claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers is governed by short-range-order evolution within the FCC layers.
Controlled thermal cycling can increase short-range order in the FCC layers.
Increasing short-range order enhances local lattice distortion.
The lattice distortions associated with increased short-range order impede dislocation motion.
Increased short-range order delays the onset of plastic flow.
Increased short-range order reduces the creep rate.
The proposed multilayers contain a CoCrFeMnNi-based FCC component.
The initial FCC/BCC HEA multilayers have a homogeneous chemical distribution.
Short-range-order evolution creates additional dislocation-pinning sites in the FCC layers.
Enhanced short-range order creates a chemically inhomogeneous local environment.
The chemically inhomogeneous environment produced by short-range order raises the energy barrier for dislocation nucleation.
The chemically inhomogeneous environment produced by short-range order raises the energy barrier for dislocation mobility.
Thermally cycled multilayers will have a higher threshold for the onset of plasticity than untreated multilayers.
Thermally cycled multilayers will have a lower instantaneous creep rate than untreated multilayers.
Thermally cycled multilayers will exhibit increased local ordering in their FCC layers.
The proposed response applies only when thermal treatment does not cause grain growth, phase transformation, or alteration of the multilayer architecture.
